title: Applied ML & Evals Integrated Playbook - Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, Regression
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's end-to-end applied ML and evals practice for onboarding models to the Eval Harness, maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, applying quality guardrails, creating quantization profiles, and executing regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML researchers, and Platform owners responsible for model serving quality and cost-performance tradeoffs.

Scope and goals:
- Provide a single, repeatable process for model evaluation and onboarding that minimizes production regressions.
- Maintain canonical prompt sets and benchmarks that reflect product workloads and edge cases.
- Define quality guardrails and thresholds tied to alerting and rollout gates.
- Capture recommended quantization profiles for common model families and workloads.
- Provide a standardized regression triage and remediation workflow.

Ownership and roles:
- Applied ML (Primary): owns eval design, prompt sets, and quality guardrails.
- Serving Runtime (Secondary): provides perf profiles, kernel/quantization compatibility, and runtime metrics.
- Platform SRE: implements alerting, SLOs, and observability hooks.
- Product Owners & Solutions Eng: provide product-specific success criteria and key prompt examples.

Key components (high level):
1) Eval Harness: automated framework that runs unit, regression, and benchmark suites against model candidates. Integrates with CI, model registry, and rollout tooling.
2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: curated input sets grouped by intent, difficulty, and severity (S0-S3).
3) Model Onboarding Guide: checklist and automated tests required before a model is approved for serving.
4) Quality Guardrails: metric thresholds, automated checks, and human review gates to prevent quality regressions.
5) Quantization Profiles: recommended bit-widths and calibration settings per model family and workload.
6) Regression Triage Playbook: step-by-step response plan when a regression is detected.

Eval Harness - Standards and Best Practices:
- Test types: unit tests (deterministic token outputs for core prompts), behavioral tests (semantic correctness, safety), production-sampled A/B tests, and cost/perf benchmarks.
- CI integration: every model PR must run the eval harness with a defined budget (default: "smoke" + "full" suites depending on change size).
- Deterministic seeds and environment: specify RNG seeds, tokenizer versions, and config YAML to ensure reproducibility.
- Output artifacts: store per-run metrics (jsonl), diffs, seed logs, and rand-seed used in model-registry.

Prompt Sets & Benchmarks:
- Cataloging: prompts organized by product area (chat, summarization, rerank), difficulty (easy/med/hard), and severity (S0 trivial -> S3 critical).
- Ownership: each product area has a prompt-owner (ROTA every 6 months) who approves additions/retirements.
- Example schema (flat fields): id, intent, input, expected_behavior, difficulty, severity, owner, tags.
- Maintenance cadence: monthly light review; full audit quarterly.

Quality Guardrails (metrics and thresholds):
- Core metrics (examples):
  - Correctness score (automated eval metric normalized 0-1) - SLO: >= 0.88 for major product flows.
  - Safety filter pass rate - SLO: >= 0.995.
  - Latency P95 (production route) - SLO: <= 1200 ms.
  - Token cost per request (estimate) - alert if +20% vs baseline.
  - Regression delta (metric) - block rollout if drop > 2 points absolute on core metric.

Config table (text):
| metric | monitor | warning threshold | block threshold | owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| correctness_score | eval-harness | drop >= 1% | drop >= 2 points | Applied ML |
| safety_pass_rate | safety-automations | < 99.7% | < 99.5% | Security/Applied ML |
| latency_p95 | prod-metrics | increase 15% | increase 25% | Serving Runtime |
| cost_per_request | billing-metrics | +10% | +20% | Finance/Applied ML |

Model Onboarding Checklist (must pass before canary):
1. Model card completed with architecture, training data summary, license, and pedigree.
2. Eval harness smoke tests pass (unit + top-10 product prompts).
3. Full eval suite run completed and metrics recorded in model-registry.
4. Quantization profile recommendations tested (if applicable) with perf & quality deltas documented.
5. Security & safety review completed (bias checks, PII leakage heuristics).
6. Performance check: latency & throughput within target on representative hardware.
7. Rollout plan with canary percentage, rollback criteria, and monitoring dashboard links.

Quantization Profiles Guidance:
- Approach: prefer per-layer mixed-precision profiles where supported. Default profiles:
  - FP16 baseline (no quant) - quality baseline.
  - 8-bit symmetric per-channel (INT8) - recommended for Llama-family derivates where supported.
  - 4-bit QKV-aware (NF4/OPT-style) - use only after targeted eval and regression testing.
- Calibration: use 10k representative prompts sampled from product traffic mapped to prompt-set tags.
- Validation: for each profile run the full eval suite and compare: correctness_score, safety_pass_rate, and latency.
- Accept criteria: quality drop <= 1.5 points on core metric and safety unchanged; latency or cost improvement >= 15% to justify profile.

Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step):
1. Detection: alert fires from eval-harness nightly run or production monitoring (metric breach). Include run id, model version, diff artifact link, and topo.
2. Initial classification (Triage owner within 30 minutes):
   - Is this a behavioral regression (quality drop) or infra/perf regression?
   - Reproduce locally via eval-harness using identical seed and model artifact.
3. Containment actions (within 60 minutes):
   - For major-quality regressions: Pause rollout and revert to last-good model variant.
   - For performance regressions: route traffic to fallback pool or scale Dedicated capacity temporarily.
4. Root cause analysis (48 hours):
   - Compare tokenizer/model artifact diffs, quantization profiles, config changes, and infra differences.
   - Check related PRs and infra changes in last 24-72 hrs.
5. Remediation and validation (72 hours):
   - Apply fix (model-adjust, update quant profile, or infra rollback).
   - Re-run eval-harness full suite and production-sampled A/B tests.
6. Postmortem & lessons learned (7 days):
   - Publish short incident summary, RCA, and new automated checks if applicable.

Automation and CI recommendations:
- CI gates: require smoke tests to pass for merge; require full eval run for model-releases.
- Nightly jobs: run prioritized prompt-sets against production traffic sample for early drift detection.
- Artifact storage: store all eval artifacts in model-registry with immutable links referenced by rollout jobs.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Provide per-model dashboards: correctness_score time-series, safety pass rate, latency P50/P95, token_cost.
- Alerting tiers: warning (Slack), critical (PagerDuty). Include links to run artifacts in alert body.

Operational notes and frequently-encountered issues:
- Common false-positive regressions: RNG seed differences, tokenizer version drift, and dataset sampling bias. Standard checks in triage should verify tokenizer and seed.
- Quantization surprises: layer-wise overflow in FP->INT conversions; ensure layer calibration reports are inspected.

Appendix: Example CLI snippets and config YAML (text):
- Run eval harness (smoke):
  ./eval-harness run --suite smoke --model v1.2.0 --seed 42 --out artifacts/v1.2.0/smoke.jsonl
- Export artifact to model-registry:
  ./model-registry upload --model v1.2.0 --artifact artifacts/v1.2.0/smoke.jsonl --notes "pre-canary smoke"

Change history and review cadence:
- Playbook owner will review annually or after any major incident.
- Minor updates (labels, thresholds) can be changed by Applied ML owners and recorded in the model-registry changelog.

Contacts and escalation:
- Applied ML PagerDuty: applied-ml@pagerduty.redwood.com (coverage 24/7 for critical regressions).
- Serving Runtime oncall: runtime-oncall@pagerduty.redwood.com
- Product escalation: solutions-eng@redwood.com

This document should be used as the canonical cross-functional reference for all eval and model-onboarding work. Link additions, product-specific prompt sets, and audit evidence should be added as child pages under the relevant subdirectories (eval-harness, prompt-sets-and-benchmarks, model-onboarding, etc.).
